procedural_matters: The International Jury panel is composed in accordance to RRS N1.4(b).
Hearing No. 15 was heard together with hearing No. 20 in accordance with RRS 63.(2)(b) since the hearings arose from the same incident.
Diego Yubero, support person of ESP 73, attended the hearing as observer.
Manel Llige Puig and Francois Farjaud, members of the Race Committee, attended the hearing as observer.
Nicole De By, member of the International Jury, saw the incident, declared it at the beginning of the hearing and subsequently provided evidence, as permitted by RRS 63.4(d).
ESP 73 and FRA 84 provided photographic and video evidence during the hearing. Procedural matters for the reopened hearing:
The International Jury decided that it may have made a significant error in the awarding of redress and decided to reopen the hearing in accordance with RRS 63.7(a)(2).
In the reopened hearing Ilca Heinrich, member of the International Jury which was not involved in the original hearing, joined the panel in accordance to RRS 63.7(c)(2).
In the reopened hearing the International Jury was properly constituted in accordance to RRS N1.2.
As the reopened hearing was to consider the application of redress, ESP 73 was represented by support person Diego Yubero.
In the reopened hearing, Benjamin Bonnaud, support person of FRA 84, attended the hearing as observer.
facts: Race 5, 49erFX blue fleet, wind 20 kts with choppy sea.
About 10 boat lengths after rounding the top mark, ESP 73 was sailing on the run on a starboard tack with her kite hoisted.
FRA 84 was sailing on the run on a starboard tack with her kite hoisted, clear astern of ESP 73 by 5 boat lengths and leeward of ESP 73 by one boat length.
A 10-meters long vessel not racing was sailing on a beam reach on starboard tack, slowly crossing infront of ESP 73.
At that moment ESP 73’s bow was aiming at the vessel bow and the distance between the bows was about 3 boat lengths.
ESP 73 bore away and her bow was now aiming astern of the vessel.
FRA 84 and the vessel held their course.
ESP 73 was two boat lengths ahead of FRA 84 with no lateral distance and 2 boat lengths to windward of the vessel.
ESP 73 and FRA 84 sailed for two boat lengths holding their courses.
ESP 73 established an overlap one and a half boat lengths to leeward of the vessel.
FRA 84 overlapped between the vessel and ESP 73.
The lateral distance between FRA 84 and the vessel was approximately one boat length.
ESP 73 luffed.
The vessel bore away sharply.
A contact immediately occured between FRA 84’s starboard wing and the port side of the hull of the vessel, and between FRA 84’s port wing and ESP 84’s starboard wing.
FRA 84 abruptly lost speed and began nosediving.
Both boats capsized at the same time.
The contact caused a crack to the front edge of centerboard of ESP 73.
The contact also caused a cut in FRA 84’s sail and a 40cm hole to FRA 84 hull.
A crew member of ESP 73 had a contusion to her leg.
Neither boat took any penalty.
Both boats finished the race.
FRA 84 scored 9th in race 4, 10th in race 6 and 2nd in race 7.
ESP 73 scored 13rd in race 4, 4th in race 6 and 8th in race 7.
New facts for the reopening:
When FRA 84 capsized, she lost approximately 14 places.
When ESP 73 capsized, she lost approximately 11 places.

conclusions: FRA 84 to windward failed to keep clear of ESP 37 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
Since FRA 84 broke RRS 11 while she was sailing within the room to which she was entitled by RRS 19.2(b), she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(b) for this breach.
When changing course, ESP 37 the right-of-way boat gave FRA 84 room to keep clear and did not break RRS 16.1.
ESP 37 gave FRA 84 room at the obstruction and did not break RRS 19.2(b).
The vessel not racing was right-of-way but did not keep her course and speed by sharply bearing away, therefore she broke IRPCAS rule 17(a)(1).
The collision was casued by the alteration of the course of the vessel not racing into the room that was correctly given by ESP 37 and used by FRA 84.
It was not reasonably possible for ESP 37, the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with FRA 84 when it became clear that FRA 84 was not keeping clear. ESP 37 did not break RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for FRA 84 to avoid contact with ESP 37. FRA 84 did not break RRS 14(a).

ESP 37’s score in race 5 was made significantly worse through the capsize and not by physical damage caused by the action of a vessel not racing that was determined to be at fault under the IRPCAS. Therefore the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(3) are not met.

FRA 84’s score in race 5 was made significantly worse through the capsize and not by physical damage and injury because of the action of a vessel not racing that was determined to be at fault under the IRPCAS. Therefore the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(3) are not met.
